set_aside.subject: viewer access-link entry rate limit
set_aside.question: What exact viewer-entry attempts are limited, by which key, over what window and threshold, and what observable failure is returned when the limit is exceeded?
options: Limit by source address, counting all entry attempts
Limit by access-link credential or viewer, counting failed attempts
Apply combined per-address and per-credential limits
set_aside.default_guess: Use combined per-source-address and per-credential limits, count failed attempts, and return a concealed rate-limit response.

witness.initial: A valid viewer access credential exists, and many invalid credential submissions have already arrived from one source address.
events: The viewer submits the valid credential from that same source address.
outcomes: The entry is refused because the source-address limit is exhausted.
The entry succeeds because attempts are limited by credential and the valid credential has no exhausted counter.
witness.observer: The viewer and the deployment operator

set_aside.subject: viewer sign-out origin validation
set_aside.text: a viewer sign-out is refused unless it comes from the portal's own public origin
set_aside.question: What evidence establishes that a sign-out comes from the portal's own public origin, which configured origin or origins qualify, and what happens when the request has no Origin header?
options: Require an exact Origin-header match to one canonical configured public origin
Accept an exact match to any configured trusted origin
Use Origin when present and Referer as a fallback
Accept an absent Origin and reject only an explicit mismatch
set_aside.default_guess: Require an exact Origin-header match to the single configured public origin and refuse missing or mismatched headers.

witness.initial: A viewer has a valid session cookie.
events: A client sends the sign-out request with that cookie but without an Origin header.
outcomes: The portal refuses sign-out and leaves the session active.
The portal accepts sign-out because no conflicting cross-origin evidence was supplied and ends the session.

set_aside.subject: lazy manual budget creation during progress read
set_aside.text: creates that empty manual budget version
set_aside.question: What activation state and relationship to any existing budget versions does the newly created empty manual budget version have, especially when an imported snapshot is already active?
options: Create an inactive manual version and preserve the currently active budget version
Create and activate the manual version, deactivating any active snapshot
Create the manual version only when no budget version of any source is active
set_aside.default_guess: Create one inactive manual version and leave any active imported snapshot unchanged.

witness.initial: An archived project has an active approved-estimate snapshot, no manual budget version, and an existing staff assignment.
events: The assigned staff member reads the project's progress list.
outcomes: An inactive empty manual version is stored while the imported snapshot remains the client-visible active budget.
The empty manual version becomes active and the imported snapshot is deactivated, changing the client-visible budget because of a read.
witness.observer: Assigned staff and the client viewer

set_aside.subject: progress-list read when lazy budget creation fails
set_aside.text: a staff read of a project's progress list, when the project has no manual budget version yet, creates that empty manual budget version
set_aside.question: If the manual-budget write cannot be completed, must the progress-list read fail atomically, or may it return progress without creating the promised version?
options: Fail the whole read and create nothing
Return the progress list without a manual version and retry initialization on a later read
Return the progress list with an explicit initialization warning
set_aside.default_guess: Fail the whole read atomically and create nothing.

witness.initial: An archived project has no manual budget version, its progress records are readable, and storage rejects creation of a manual budget version.
events: An assigned staff member requests the progress list.
outcomes: The request fails because its required lazy initialization failed.
The existing progress list is returned even though no manual budget version was created.

set_aside.subject: concurrent lazy manual budget creation
set_aside.text: when the project has no manual budget version yet, creates that empty manual budget version
set_aside.question: Is lazy creation guaranteed to produce exactly one manual budget version per project under retries or concurrent progress reads, and do all such reads resolve to that same version?
options: Enforce one manual budget version per project and make creation atomic/idempotent
Allow multiple manual versions but designate one deterministically
set_aside.default_guess: Enforce a single manual budget version per project with atomic idempotent creation.

witness.initial: An archived project has no manual budget version and two authorized staff sessions can read it.
events: Both staff members request the progress list concurrently before either creation commits.
outcomes: Both reads resolve to one shared newly created manual budget version.
Each read creates a distinct empty manual budget version.
witness.observer: Staff inspecting the budget history, audit records, or later progress state
